title: A bakery's cake plan
body: A home bakery makes two kinds of cakes. One cake of Type I needs 200 g of flour and 25 g of fat. One cake of Type II needs 100 g of flour and 50 g of fat. On a particular day the bakery has 5 kg of flour and 1 kg of fat, and no other ingredient is in short supply. Let x be the number of Type I cakes and y the number of Type II cakes made that day. The owner wants to plan the day's baking so that the flour and fat limits are not exceeded and the total number of cakes made is as large as possible. She decides to write the problem as a linear programming problem and solve it by the graphical (corner point) method.
